newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on profit-taking.

text.p: Most Shanghai copper futures contracts ended down on Thursday on profit-taking, after overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active June 1997 contract ended at 23,350 yuan ($2,814) per tonne, losing 200 yuan. It opened at 23,300 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,400 and a low of 20,260.
March, the only rising contract, put on 40 yuan to 23,190, April fell 110 to 23,250, May 190 to 23,330, July 150 to 23,350 and August 260 to 23,290.
Combined volume rose to 57,860 tonnes from 45,870.
Aluminium ended mostly down. March, the only contract to rise, gained 20 yuan to 16,020, April fell 80 to 16,220 and May 80 to 16,530.
Combined volume fell to 2,000 tonnes from 3,090.
Copper opened lower and moved at low levels for most of the session.
Traders said profit-taking still dominated Thursday's trading.
"Most investors don't believe there will be a correction in the copper price any time soon, so they prefer to liquidate their positions at high levels," one trader said.
Traders said copper was likely to consolidate around the current level, with most investors waiting for market-moving news.
